```{r}
#| include: false

## Home page ("Night and Day" design): hero with the featured figure,
## three audience doors (linking to the sections of join.qmd, the Get
## involved page), research theme cards, the navy "How we work"
## track-record band, latest papers, team teaser, then Joshua's bio and
## Connect links. Built from Pandoc markdown (fenced divs and spans); styles
## are in styles/bml.scss and styles/bml-home.scss. The page has no title
## (so no title banner): the hero's .bml-display is the page heading.

## load packages and setup
source("package_setup.R", echo = FALSE)

## ---- track record (stats band and bio), all from the CV spreadsheet and
## all rounded down (belowRound) so the page never overclaims ----
## The bio is an official bio, so it opens with the official title
## ("Associate Professor Joshua Wiley"); general mentions say "Dr Joshua Wiley".
position <- currentPosition()
grantMillions <- belowRound(ciGrantTotalAUD() / 1e6, 1)
pubs <- as.data.table(read_excel(cvpath, sheet = "Publications"))
nPubs <- belowRound(nrow(pubs), 10)

## citations from every source in the Citations sheet (for the stats band)
citeSources <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(c("Google Scholar", "Scopus"), getCitations))

## downloads of all the lab's R packages (Posit's CRAN mirror); NULL if none
downloads <- getDownloads()

## the stats band: number and label for each figure we have
stat <- function(num, label) list(num = num, label = label)
cites <- setNames(lapply(citeSources, function(x) fmtNum(belowRound(x$total, 1000))),
                  vapply(citeSources, `[[`, "", "source"))
stats <- list(
  stat(sprintf("\\>%d", nPubs), "publications"),
  stat(sprintf("\\>\\$%dM", grantMillions), "AUD in competitive funding as chief investigator"),
  if (!is.null(cites[["Google Scholar"]])) stat(
    sprintf("\\>%s", cites[["Google Scholar"]]),
    sprintf("citations on Google Scholar%s",
            if (!is.null(cites[["Scopus"]])) sprintf(" (\\>%s Scopus)", cites[["Scopus"]]) else ""))
  else if (!is.null(cites[["Scopus"]])) stat(sprintf("\\>%s", cites[["Scopus"]]), "citations on Scopus"),
  if (!is.null(downloads)) stat(
    sprintf("\\>%s", fmtNum(belowRound(downloads$total, 10000))),
    sprintf("downloads of our %d R packages", downloads$packages)))
stats <- Filter(Negate(is.null), stats)

## "as of October 2026": the month of the citation and download counts (the
## publication and funding figures are read live at render time)
asOfMonths <- unique(na.omit(c(
  vapply(citeSources, function(x) format(x$asOf, "%B %Y"), ""),
  if (!is.null(downloads) && !is.na(downloads$asOf)) format(downloads$asOf, "%B %Y"))))
if (length(asOfMonths) == 0) asOfMonths <- format(Sys.Date(), "%B %Y")
statsNote <- sprintf(
  "Track record of Dr Joshua Wiley, as of %s, rounded down.%s",
  paste(asOfMonths, collapse = " and "),
  if (!is.null(downloads)) " Downloads from the Posit CRAN mirror." else "")

## ---- people (doors and team teaser), from readPeople() ----
counts <- labCounts()
currentTypes <- readPeople()[Status == "Current", Type]
membersText <- sprintf(
  if (all(grepl("^(Postdoctoral|PhD|DPsych|Masters|Honours)", currentTypes)))
    "%d postdocs and students" else "%d members", counts$current)

## papers the lab leads (Joshua first or last author) with a trainee as
## first author; "Most ..." only when that is true
labLed <- pubs[FirstLast == 1 & Type %in% c("Empirical", "Review", "Protocol")]
studentShare <- labLed[, mean(StudentFirst %in% 1)]
studentText <- if (nrow(labLed) > 0 && studentShare > .5)
  " Most papers the lab leads have a student as first author." else ""

## ---- research themes: the frozen snapshot (see CLAUDE.md) ----
research <- readResearch()
themes <- research$themes

## the plate: the insomnia trial (as in the design), or else the first theme
## whose exemplar has a figure
heroId <- "INSOMNIA"
hasFigure <- vapply(themes, function(t) !is.null(t$exemplar$figure), TRUE)
ids <- vapply(themes, `[[`, "", "id")
hero <- if (heroId %in% ids[hasFigure]) which(ids == heroId) else which(hasFigure)[1]

## theme cards: the plate's theme first, then the rest in order
cardOrder <- c(hero, setdiff(seq_along(themes), hero))
numWords <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
allThemes <- if (length(themes) <= 10) numWords[length(themes)] else length(themes)

## ---- latest papers ----
latest <- latestPublications(4)
```

}

::: {.grid .bml-theme-cards}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

## one card per theme: its exemplar's figure (or the finding alone), the
## theme's name, the plain-language finding, then the citation and "Read more",
## which makes the whole card a link to the paper. The first two are wide; on phones only
## the first three show, then "All five themes". Each card keeps its theme's
## id (#stress, ...), which used to be the home page's theme sections.
for (k in seq_along(cardOrder)) {
  t <- themes[[cardOrder[k]]]
  p <- t$exemplar
  wide <- k <= 2
  media <- if (!is.null(p$figure)) sprintf(
    '::: {.bml-card-media%s}\n%s\n\n%s\n:::\n',
    if (wide) " .bml-media-lg" else "", paperFigureMd(p, link = FALSE), paperCredit(p)) else ""
  cat(sprintf('
::: {#%s .g-col-12 .g-col-md-6%s .bml-card .bml-card-flush .bml-theme-card%s}
%s
::: {.bml-card-body}
[%s]{.bml-eyebrow .bml-muted}

[%s]{.%s}

::: {.bml-card-foot}
[%s (%s)]{} [[Read more\\ [→]{aria-hidden="true"}](%s){.stretched-link aria-label="Read more: %s (%s), %s"}]{}
:::
:::
:::
',
    t$anchor, if (wide) "" else " .g-col-lg-4", if (k > 3) " .bml-phone-extra" else "",
    media, mdEscape(t$short), mdEscape(p$summary),
    if (wide) "bml-finding" else "bml-finding-sm",
    mdEscape(paperAuthor(p)), p$year, paperDoi(p),
    attrEscape(paperAuthor(p)), p$year, attrEscape(p$title)))
}
```

## How we work {#how-we-work}

Randomised trials of brief and digital treatments, intensive daily studies with phones, wearables and at-home sleep recordings, and new statistical methods we share as free software.

}
cat(sprintf("::: {.bml-stat-note}\n%s\n:::\n:::\n", statsNote))

## Latest from the lab {#latest}
:::

[All publications\ [→]{aria-hidden="true"}](cv.qmd#publications){.bml-link}
:::

::: {.grid}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

## the newest papers from the Publications sheet: label and year, title
## (linked to the DOI; the whole card is the link), first author and journal.
## If a reference can't be parsed, the card shows the reference itself.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(latest))) {
  x <- latest[i]
  url <- if (!is.na(x$DOI)) x$DOI else "cv.qmd#publications"
  head <- if (!is.na(x$Title)) {
    sprintf("[[%s](%s){.stretched-link}]{.bml-title-sm}", x$Title, url)
  } else {
    sprintf("[%s [Read the paper](%s){.stretched-link}]{.bml-cite}", x$Reference, url)
  }
  src <- paste(na.omit(c(x$Author, x$Journal)), collapse = ", ")
  cat(sprintf('
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .g-col-lg-3 .bml-card .bml-latest}
[%s · %d]{.bml-eyebrow}

%s

%s
:::
', x$Kind, as.integer(x$Year), head,
    if (nzchar(src) && !is.na(x$Title)) sprintf("[%s]{.bml-meta .bml-push}", src) else ""))
}
```

## Joshua F. Wiley {#joshua-f.-wiley}
:::

[`r position`, School of Psychological Sciences and Turner Institute for Brain and Mental Health, Monash University]{.bml-meta}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-lg-8 .bml-bio-text}
`r position` Joshua Wiley leads the Behavioural Medicine Lab at Monash
University and is an Honorary Research Fellow at the Peter MacCallum Cancer
Centre. He completed a PhD in health psychology at the University of
California, Los Angeles, followed by postdoctoral training in randomised
controlled trials.

His research follows how sleep, stress and emotions unfold in daily life,
then uses those findings to build accessible sleep and emotion-regulation
interventions. His group pairs data from phones and wearables with modern
statistics and shares new methods and tools as free software. His work has
been funded by the NHMRC, MRFF and ARC, the US National Institutes of
Health and Department of Defense, and the Wellcome Trust.
